Lieth
lī´ĕth
v. (third person singular of lie: to recline, remain, be situated; rendering Hebrew rabats and shakab, Greek keimai)
Old English licgan, to lie down. The Authorized Version's -eth form of lie in the sense of resting along a surface; the AV also has the other lie, to speak falsely (“lieth concerning it,” Lev 6:3), a different word by descent.

Biblical Definition

Something lieth when it rests where it has been laid. “Sin lieth at the door” (Gen 4:7) — the Hebrew is the crouching of an animal. “The whole world lieth in wickedness” (1Jn 5:19) — John's verb is a posture, the world lying in the wicked one as a man lies in a bed. Job says, “man lieth down, and riseth not: till the heavens be no more” (Job 14:12). Paul measures a duty by it: “as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men” (Rom 12:18). And the last city “lieth foursquare” (Rev 21:16). Of the sick: “my servant lieth at home sick of the palsy” (Mat 8:6).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines lie as to be extended on a surface, to rest; to be situated; to remain in a state or condition.

expand to see more

LIE, v.i. To be in a horizontal position, or nearly so, and to rest on any thing lengthwise; to rest in a reclining posture.

2. To be situated; as, the land lies on the east.

3. To remain in a state or condition; to be laid up; to lie in wait; to lie at the mercy of.

Key Scripture

Gen 4:7 — "If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door. And unto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule over him."

1Jn 5:19 — "And we know that we are of God, and the whole world lieth in wickedness."

Rom 12:18 — "If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men."

Job 14:12 — "So man lieth down, and riseth not: till the heavens be no more, they shall not awake, nor be raised out of their sleep."

Rev 21:16 — "And the city lieth foursquare, and the length is as large as the breadth: and he measured the city with the reed, twelve thousand furlongs. The length and the breadth and the height of it are equal."

Psa 41:8 — "An evil disease, say they, cleaveth fast unto him: and now that he lieth he shall rise up no more."

Modern Corruption

The world lying in wickedness is softened into a world with problems, and Genesis 4:7 is preached as a promise of willpower.

expand to see more

First John 5:19 is a verse about position. “We know that we are of God, and the whole world lieth in wickedness” — two places, no third. The world is not described as struggling, drifting, or mixed; it lies in the wicked one the way a body lies in a bed, because that is where it rests. Modern religion prefers a world that is basically well-meaning and occasionally mistaken, and it reads John's verb as a mood. John meant a posture, and the only way out of the posture is to be “of God,” which is birth, not improvement.

Genesis 4:7 is God's warning to Cain before the first murder: “if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door. And unto thee shall be his desire, and thou shalt rule over him.” The verb is the crouching of a beast (the same word describes Issachar “couching down between two burdens,” Gen 49:14), and the verse is commonly preached as a promise of mastery: sin is waiting, but you can rule it. Cain is the answer to that reading. The man warned went straight out into the field and did it. The command exposes the inability; it does not confer the ability. What masters sin is not resolve but grace — “sin shall not have dominion over you: for ye are not under the law, but under grace” (Rom 6:14).

Romans 12:18 gives the word its honest limit. “If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men” — Paul does not promise peace with everyone, because peace takes two. He commands everything that lies in the believer's part and leaves the other man's part where it lies.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew rabats (H7257), to crouch, couch; shakab (H7901), to lie down; Greek keimai (G2749), to lie, be laid.

expand to see more

Hebrew rabats (H7257) — to crouch as an animal; Genesis 4:7, Genesis 49:9, 49:14.

Hebrew shakab (H7901) — to lie down, to lie with; Job 14:12, Psalm 41:8, Leviticus 15:4.

Greek keimai (G2749) — to lie, be laid, be set; 1 John 5:19, Revelation 21:16, Luke 2:12.

Greek ballo, passive (G906) — laid, thrown down; Matthew 8:6, “lieth at home sick of the palsy.”

Usage

"“Sin lieth at the door” — a beast couching, and a man who did not rule it."

"“The whole world lieth in wickedness” — a posture, not a mood."

"“As much as lieth in you” — the measure of your own part in peace."
